title: Observable travel persona matched pairs
purpose: Measure whether a simulated traveller expresses one task-relevant persona attribute at a time while preserving every original Odysseys requirement.

arm_labels.positive: The focal/high-expression pole used for the controlled contrast.
arm_labels.negative: The opposite comparison pole. Negative is an experimental label, not a quality judgment.

pairing_controls: Use the same original task, persona model, CUA model, judge model, prompts, runtime limits, and replicate identifier for both arms.
Within a pair, change exactly one MatrAIx dimension value; all other rendered persona dimensions and the display name remain identical.
Keep original task requirements hard: a persona pole may change emphasis or preference, but may not remove, contradict, or invent a task requirement.
Judge persona adherence from simulated-user utterances only; task success and CUA alignment remain separate axes.
invalid_pair_conditions: Either arm fails to communicate every original task rubric.
The two runs differ in more than the target persona dimension or controlled run metadata.
The only cited persona evidence is wording already required by the original task.
A run is scored on an axis-task combination not listed as applicable below.

scoring.evidence_unit: An exact or tightly paraphrased simulated-user utterance, not a CUA action or answer.

per_arm_scale.0: No supporting behavior, a direct contradiction, or behavior that violates a hard task requirement.
per_arm_scale.1: Weak or ambiguous support, including merely repeating language inherited from the original task.
per_arm_scale.2: Clear task-specific expression beyond inherited task wording, with no contradictory user behavior.

scoring.binary_adherence_rule: expressed=true if and only if the per-arm score is 2.
scoring.pair_separation_rule: A matched pair separates only when both arms score 2 for their assigned poles and the cited evidence shows meaningfully opposite preferences or behavior.
scoring.coverage_guardrail: Both arms must communicate 100% of the original task rubrics; otherwise report the pair as invalid rather than treating omission as persona expression.
reporting: Report positive-arm adherence, negative-arm adherence, and pair separation separately by axis and task.
Keep task success and CUA alignment separate; never average them into persona adherence.
Retain the cited utterance, score, confidence, task ID, profile hash, model identities, and replicate identifier for auditability.

positive.behavioral_definition: Treats the lowest defensible total cost as the deciding factor and wants prices made comparable before choosing.
generic_observables: Asks for the cheapest qualifying option and for the total, not just a headline rate.
Wants fees, taxes or per-person costs surfaced so options compare like for like.
Says an upgrade is only worth it when the extra money is justified explicitly.
contradictions: Chooses a costlier option for comfort or prestige when a qualifying cheaper one is available.
Says the price difference does not matter.

negative.behavioral_definition: Treats quality, comfort and a better experience as the deciding factor and accepts paying more within the task's stated limits.
generic_observables: Asks for the best-regarded or most comfortable qualifying option rather than the cheapest.
Says it is fine to spend up to the stated ceiling if the experience is better.
Prioritises ratings, location or class of service over saving money.
contradictions: Optimises for the lowest total cost when a better qualifying option fits the stated limit.
Asks to cut a requested comfort or quality element to save money.

ada70bfe81da1cd33bec47d79a9d279d7734a686.rationale: Two paid festive attractions are compared, so what counts as good value is the persona's to state.
inherited_task_signals: Checking what a standard Stockeld Park festive ticket includes.
Finding the official Harrogate Christmas Funland page with dates and location.
Pulling York Maze visitor details as a backup.
positive_observables: Asks which option gives more per pound and for ticket prices to be stated side by side.
Asks whether the cheaper option still counts as a full day out.
negative_observables: Says the pricier attraction is fine if the day feels better for the children.
Asks which option is the nicer experience regardless of the ticket gap.

b21a86441ddca8186175bfffcaae0358ed66eec4.rationale: Flights under a time constraint and a hotel under a nightly cap both carry visible prices.
inherited_task_signals: Searching roundtrip PIT-LAX with the stated arrival and return limits.
Finding a Koreatown or West Hollywood hotel rated 4.5+ under the nightly cap.
Sequencing the two-day itinerary around rush hour.
positive_observables: Asks for the cheapest flight and hotel pair that still meets the stated limits.
Asks to stay well under the nightly cap rather than near it.
negative_observables: Says the nightly cap may be used in full for a better-located or better-rated hotel.
Asks for the shortest or most comfortable qualifying flight even at a higher fare.

73c63095aeed43efb10a74eee7db7459c5ea9f84.rationale: The task explicitly compares a normal rental against cheaper live-in alternatives.
inherited_task_signals: Finding a Zillow rental inside the stated monthly range.
Finding at least three cheaper live-in Craigslist listings below that benchmark.
Summarising a Booking.com hotel's guest reviews.
positive_observables: Asks how far below the Zillow benchmark the alternatives actually land.
Asks for total move-in cost, not just the monthly rent.
negative_observables: Says the normal rental is worth its premium over the cheaper alternatives.
Asks which option is the most comfortable place to actually live.

positive.behavioral_definition: Actively asks for inspectable, current evidence and distinguishes confirmed facts from uncertain claims.
generic_observables: Requests first-party or live-page evidence beyond simply naming a source.
Asks the assistant to label uncertainty, stale information or unsupported claims.
Checks that a conclusion follows from the cited page rather than accepting it at face value.
contradictions: Explicitly delegates factual verification without wanting evidence.
Treats an unsupported snippet as sufficient after uncertainty has been raised.

negative.behavioral_definition: Delegates reasonable verification to the assistant and accepts its synthesis once the task's required evidence is present.
generic_observables: Explicitly says the assistant may use its judgment after the named sources have been checked.
Accepts the assistant's synthesis without asking for extra triangulation beyond the task.
Prefers a straightforward recommendation over an additional verification pass.
contradictions: Demands independent corroboration beyond the original task.
Challenges a supported result solely because it lacks an additional source.

ada70bfe81da1cd33bec47d79a9d279d7734a686.rationale: Festive event pages go stale between seasons, so currency of evidence is observable.
inherited_task_signals: Using the official Stockeld Park and Harrogate Christmas Funland pages.
Confirming the listing is live before relying on it.
Leaving the key ticket and event pages open.
positive_observables: Asks for confirmation that the event page is for this season and still live.
Asks that what is included be quoted from the page rather than summarised.
negative_observables: Says the assistant may pick the most official-looking listing it finds.
Accepts the comparison without asking how each page was confirmed.

b6b8ad71aa3112840790066d7d62b498babdfa5c.rationale: Forecasts and active alerts are time-sensitive and come from several named sources.
inherited_task_signals: Reporting current Baltimore conditions.
Reading the Syracuse 7-day low on Wunderground.
Checking the NWS Rittman forecast and active alerts, and the Mount Holly snowfall graphic.
positive_observables: Asks whether each figure is the current reading and when it was issued.
Asks that the alert text be quoted from the NWS page rather than paraphrased.
negative_observables: Says the assistant may summarise the forecast in its own words.
Accepts the risk verdict without asking to see the alert page.

795bfe117e0f58e49ca37ae8e453a507859a2a2b.rationale: Displayed prices and live listings are exactly what can be stale here.
inherited_task_signals: Finding a Booking.com London hotel under the stated total for two nights.
Recording the NOX Hotel comparison price.
Finding two DC hotels meeting the rating and price rules, and three Amazon ANC options.
positive_observables: Asks that every price be the total actually displayed for those dates, taxes included.
Asks for confirmation that each hotel page is live rather than cached.
negative_observables: Says the assistant may use its judgment on which listing is representative.
Accepts the price list without asking how each figure was read.

73c63095aeed43efb10a74eee7db7459c5ea9f84.rationale: The task requires checking that cheaper listings are still live.
inherited_task_signals: Opening an actual Zillow rental page.
Verifying the Craigslist postings are still live.
Reporting the hotel's guest review score and recent takeaways.
positive_observables: Asks for proof each Craigslist posting is still active rather than expired.
Asks that review takeaways be quoted from recent reviews with dates.
negative_observables: Says the assistant may judge which listings look genuine.
Accepts the shortlist without asking which postings were re-checked.

positive.behavioral_definition: Is working against a near-term deadline and wants the fastest route to a decision, without dropping any requirement.
generic_observables: States that a decision is needed today or within a fixed short window.
Asks the assistant to start with whatever settles the decision soonest.
Asks to be told immediately if something will take long or block the decision.
contradictions: Says there is no hurry and the work can take as long as it needs.
Asks for extra exploration that does not move the decision forward.

negative.behavioral_definition: Has no deadline and prefers a thorough, unhurried pass over the options.
generic_observables: Says explicitly that there is no rush and the work can take its time.
Invites extra options or checks that a hurried pass would skip.
Prefers getting the choice right over getting it quickly.
contradictions: Asks for the fastest possible answer.
Says a decision has to be made within a fixed short window.

890a6880049a42684ac91a2e1809442846f9394c.rationale: The outing is described as soon, so urgency is natural to state or to disclaim.
inherited_task_signals: Finding the recommended transit route and total travel time.
Summarising the Metra BNSF line and where fares are listed.
Reporting the Aurora highs and lows for the next three days.
positive_observables: Says the outing may happen in the next day or two and asks for the route first.
Asks to be told at once if fares or schedules cannot be confirmed quickly.
negative_observables: Says the trip is not fixed yet, so the fare and schedule pages can be read properly.
Invites a look at alternative routes once the main one is covered.

b6b8ad71aa3112840790066d7d62b498babdfa5c.rationale: The decision is explicitly about driving this week.
inherited_task_signals: Reporting current Baltimore conditions.
Reporting the Syracuse 7-day low and its day.
Checking NWS Rittman alerts and the Mount Holly snowfall graphic.
positive_observables: Says the drive decision has to be made today and asks for the riskiest leg first.
Asks for a go or no-go answer as soon as the alerts are known.
negative_observables: Says the drive can wait, so every location should be checked carefully.
Invites extra days of forecast beyond the ones required.

b21a86441ddca8186175bfffcaae0358ed66eec4.rationale: A two-day trip inside the next month can be urgent or leisurely.
inherited_task_signals: Searching qualifying PIT-LAX flights.
Finding a qualifying hotel and leaving its page open.
Building the two-day itinerary around rush hour.
positive_observables: Says the flight has to be booked today before the fare moves.
Asks for the itinerary only after the bookable parts are settled.
negative_observables: Says the dates are flexible, so the flight and hotel options can be compared unhurriedly.
Invites a second pass over the itinerary once the flight is chosen.

positive.behavioral_definition: Prefers public transit and walking for getting around and wants options framed that way.
generic_observables: Asks for transit or walking routes rather than assuming a car.
Treats being near a station, stop or a walkable area as a reason to prefer an option.
Asks whether a car is needed at all before accepting one.
contradictions: Asks to plan around driving when transit or walking would serve.
Dismisses transit as impractical for this trip.

negative.behavioral_definition: Doubts public transit is worth it here and prefers driving, taxis or rideshare, while still meeting every stated requirement.
generic_observables: Asks for driving, parking, taxi or rideshare details rather than transit.
Says transit is likely slow, awkward or unreliable for this particular outing.
Treats door-to-door convenience as the reason to pick an option.
contradictions: Asks for transit routes or a station-adjacent option by preference.
Says the trip is better done without a car.

b6b8ad71aa3112840790066d7d62b498babdfa5c.rationale: The task is about whether to drive, so a transit attitude reframes it without dropping a requirement.
inherited_task_signals: Reporting current Baltimore conditions.
Reporting the Syracuse 7-day low.
Checking NWS Rittman alerts and the Mount Holly snowfall graphic.
positive_observables: Asks whether the trip could be done by train or bus if the forecast looks bad.
Says driving is the fallback rather than the plan.
negative_observables: Says driving is the only realistic way to make this trip.
Asks about road and parking conditions rather than any transit alternative.

b21a86441ddca8186175bfffcaae0358ed66eec4.rationale: The task already allows transit where it makes sense, so the preference is observable in how the days are sequenced.
inherited_task_signals: Searching qualifying PIT-LAX flights.
Finding a qualifying Koreatown or West Hollywood hotel.
Sequencing the stops to avoid rush-hour driving.
positive_observables: Asks for the itinerary built around Metro, buses or walking instead of a rental car.
Asks whether the hotel is near a transit line.
negative_observables: Asks for driving times and parking between the itinerary stops.
Says a rental car or rideshare is how the two days will actually be covered.

73c63095aeed43efb10a74eee7db7459c5ea9f84.rationale: Where to live in Grand Rapids turns on how the person expects to get around.
inherited_task_signals: Finding a Zillow rental inside the stated range.
Finding three cheaper live-in Craigslist listings.
Summarising the hotel's guest reviews.
positive_observables: Asks whether each place is walkable or on a bus route.
Says no car is planned, so car-dependent listings are less useful.
negative_observables: Asks about parking and driving times for each listing.
Says everything will be done by car, so transit access does not matter.
